ArXiv cs.AI.title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18642v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down. We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. We compare one agent that plays eight lives and keeps its whole history with a chain of eight age

ArXiv cs.AI.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18714v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18747v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior.

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Multimodal Fusion: A Review of Breast Cancer Advanced and Traditional Modalities
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18793v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Purpose: Multimodal medical imaging fusion (MMIF) is an increasingly important approach to breast cancer detection (BCD), as different imaging modalities rely on different physical principles and provide complementary information. No single modality can capture all the structural, functional, and biological information needed for accurate diagnosis and characterization. Methods: This review examines more than 15 imaging modalities used in breast cancer detection, including conventional techniques such as mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic res

ArXiv cs.AI.title: D\'ecoupage: Directorial Audio-Visual Control for Long Multi-Shot Video Generation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18866v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In cinematic storytelling, sound and visual transitions do not always coincide in lockstep: dialogue frequently bridges across cuts to reveal reactions or introduces new scenes via J- and L-cuts, while deliberate silences pace the scene. Existing audio-visual generative frameworks, however, lack explicit mechanisms to coordinate independent visual and acoustic timing over extended horizons. As narrative duration and shot complexity scale, these systems struggle to maintain long-range dialogue pacing, often hallucinating speech during intended si

ArXiv cs.AI.title: SPLICE: Structured Prompt Local Iterative Combinatorial Evolution
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18883v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Natural language optimization (NLO) improves an agent by having a model critique and rewrite its natural language policy parameters: system prompts, tool instructions, reasoning directives, few-shot demonstrations. These artifacts are multi-section documents in which some sections encode contracts (safety clauses, tool schemas, output formats) that must not drift, while others are legitimate optimization targets. Most iterative NLO methods treat the artifact as a single editable string, producing three recurrent failure modes: unsafe global rewr

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Bring Back Language to Actions: Restoring VLM capabilities in VLA Models via Parameter Merging
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18891v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) are obtained by fine-tuning pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on robot demonstration data, enabling action prediction from visual observations and language instructions. However, this fine-tuning induces catastrophic forgetting, substantially degrading the semantic and visual grounding capabilities of the original VLM. We address this by merging the parameters of a VLM and its VLA derivative without retraining either model. Concretely, we extract the task vector (the difference between VLA and VLM wei

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Ask Precisely, Assume Wisely: Interactive Evaluation of Ambiguity Resolution in Large Language Models
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18905v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ambiguity is a core challenge in human--AI interaction, where models must decide when to make assumptions and when to seek clarification. Existing approaches to ambiguity evaluation largely focus on coverage over multiple interpretations using static metrics, offering limited insight into how efficiently a model converges toward a single user-intended interpretation through interaction. We introduce a preference-grounded simulated user framework for controlled, multi-turn evaluation of ambiguity resolution, grounding simulator responses strictly

ArXiv cs.AI.title: MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18908v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxo

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Between Rigor and Reality: How AI Safety Benchmark Developers Understand Benchmark Use and Maintenance
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18930v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Safety benchmarks are cited as the primary tool to understand the risks posed by generative AI (GenAI) systems, yet growing evidence suggests they often fail to meet the needs of real-world safety evaluation. We present findings from five interviews with AI safety benchmark developers in academia and industry. We find a disconnect between perceptions of the intended usefulness of safety benchmarks and their practical usefulness in safety evaluations of deployed systems. Our participants offered perspectives on two challenges contributing to this

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Dual-Stage Channel-Posterior Integration for MLM-Aided Token Communications
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18958v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Token transmission over conventional digital modulation is vulnerable to channel impairments, leading to bit errors that cause received tokens to become contextually inconsistent. This paper proposes a receiver-side dual-stage channel-posterior integration framework for masked language model (MLM)-aided token reconstruction. In the proposed framework, the receiver detects unreliable token positions from channel reliability and constructs a vocabulary-level channel-posterior. In particular, within the receiver, Posterior-Weighted Input Embedding

ArXiv cs.AI.title: SpecRelay: Amortize or Avoid the Round Trip in Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18963v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Edge-cloud speculative decoding moves autoregressive drafting to an edge device while a larger cloud model verifies draft tokens in parallel, so that edge drafting and cloud verification overlap under a synchronous draft-verify schedule. Beyond low-latency local networks, however, the next verification request of that schedule can be sent only after the previous reply arrives, so every round still waits out a full round trip, and throughput falls as the network RTT grows. To recover this loss, we present SpecRelay, an edge-cloud LLM inference sy

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Three Invisible Failure Modes in Speech-Based Age Estimation for Child Safety
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.18971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated whether three audio-capable large language models can predict a child's age from their speech across five studies using two speech corpora of children under the age of 13. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Match and Correct: A Repeated Computational Motif in Evoformer Layers
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.19016v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Triangle attention and triangle multiplicative updates form key components of the Evoformer, and were introduced specifically to encourage consistency with the triangle inequality. Yet whether representational changes over layers reduce triangle inequality violations has not been tested. We probe the pair representation at each of OpenFold's 48 Evoformer layers, decoding final C$_\alpha$-C$_\alpha$ distances with four probe families (a shared linear probe, per-protein linear probes, a sequence-separation-gated linear probe, and XGBoost) and reco

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Large Language Models for AI Infrastructure
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.19061v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to design, optimize, and operate the infrastructure behind AI training and serving, yet the literature remains fragmented across hardware design, machine learning systems, electronic design automation, and high-performance computing. We present a comprehensive survey of LLM-assisted AI infrastructure across its lifecycle, from accelerator design and kernel engineering to compilation, deployment, operations, data management, and energy optimization. We organize the literature by the primary resou

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Check Token: Real-Time Self-Verification and Precise Truncation in LLM Reasoning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18564v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: ECC memory embeds 8 parity bits for every 64 data bits and automatically detects and corrects errors on each read. The parity bits carry no data and only safeguard integrity, at ~12.5% overhead. Yet the reasoning chains of large language models lack such built-in self-verification: once an error occurs it propagates along the chain, and existing methods can only verify externally after generation completes. We propose the check token, establishing built-in self-verification for language model generation streams for the first time: a functional m

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Quantize, Qualify, Rerank: A Recipe for Compressing LLMs Without Losing Quality
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18587v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Compressing large language models lowers serving cost, but a single automatic metric may miss quality loss. For the WMT26 Model Compression constrained track, we compress google/gemma-3-12b-it (24.4 GB in bf16) for three translation directions on one H100. Paired bootstrap analysis exposes metric disagreement on 4-bit quantization; guided by WMT24 human meta-evaluation, we use MetricX24-XXL as primary and CometKiwi-XXL as a cross-check. Removing the unused vision stack and non-task vocabulary and using int8 weights or fp8 activations causes no r

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Skill-Latent Rewards: LLM-Guided Reward Formulation for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18597v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon reinforcement learning under sparse and delayed feedback remains an open challenge. Existing return-decomposition methods redistribute episodic rewards to ease credit assignment, but they operate on raw state--action transitions and disregard the subgoal structure that governs meaningful progress in complex tasks. We propose Skill-LR, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework in which a vision--language model identifies the agent's active subgoal at each timestep and a large language model generates a matching latent reward fo

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Not All Data Leakage Is Equal: A Controlled Benchmark of Evaluation Inflation in Tabular Classification
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18598v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Data leakage is widely recognized as a threat to trustworthy machine-learning evaluation, yet the phrase covers mechanisms with very different statistical consequences. We present a controlled empirical benchmark that measures the inflation in held-out ROC-AUC caused by five common leakage mechanisms: global standardization, global median imputation, duplicate contamination, supervised feature selection before splitting, and target encoding before splitting. The benchmark spans six public datasets and two synthetic stress tests, three model fami

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Mambas Selective Gate in Financial Markets: A Leakage-Controlled Study
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18599v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Selectively gated state-space models (SSMs), notably Mamba, are increasingly used for financial time series, yet how they internally represent market regimes (bull, bear, sideways) remains opaque. This paper applies Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) to a six-layer Mamba trained on approximately twenty-one years of daily data for a point-in-time set of S&P 500 constituents plus macroeconomic and Fama-French factors, decomposing per-layer hidden states with Top-K Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs). Our central contribution is methodological and cautionary

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Multimodal Fusion with Pre-trained Models for Psychotherapy Outcome Prediction from Emotional Dynamics
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In-session emotional dynamics are associated with psychotherapy outcomes but difficult to measure at scale. Pretrained multimodal models provide automated access to facial, vocal, and textual signals, yet clinical datasets remain small. Our research question is how pretrained multimodal representations can best support psychotherapy outcome prediction under data scarcity. Three studies use 106 sessions from 88 patients and nine session-level outcome scales (HSCL-11, EPO-1, POMS). Study 1 asks whether deep learning outperforms classical machine l

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Predictive maintenance in manufacturing: The operational value of continual machine learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18636v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Predictive maintenance in high-volume manufacturing often faces a domain-incremental learning problem: as new product configurations enter production, prediction models must learn from newly available data while preserving performance on earlier configurations that remain in operation. In this paper, we empirically study the operational value of continual machine learning methods for addressing this challenge in predictive maintenance, using real-world maintenance data from Bosch. The setting at Bosch covers 25 product configurations over five y

ArXiv cs.LG.title: GRAFT: Cross-Backbone LoRA Reuse for Continual Language and Multimodal Learning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18638v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In continual learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning enables large language models to acquire new capabilities through lightweight adapters such as LoRA, yet the reuse of pretrained adapters is typically restricted to models sharing the same backbone. This limits the transfer of learned capabilities from language models to multimodal models. We propose GRAFT (Generalist Reuse of Adapters via Feature-space Transfer), a framework for cross-backbone LoRA reuse. GRAFT retrieves the most relevant pretrained LoRA adapter from a modality-aware librar

ArXiv cs.LG.title: SynthDCB: World Distillation for Scalable Device Control Benchmarking
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18639v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scaling device-control evaluation requires scaling both the worlds agents interact with and the tasks they must solve. We introduce SynthDCB, a scalable benchmark for environment awareness and device control built through world distillation. World distillation transforms knowledge of device behaviors, interaction constraints, and environmental effects into modular executable components, which are composed into interactive worlds with explicit states, actions, and temporal dynamics. A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, wor

ArXiv cs.LG.title: SERAG: SEmantical and Relational approach for Anomaly detection on knowledge Graphs
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge graphs constructed from text can contain facts that are individually plausible yet inconsistent with their relational context. We introduce SERAG, a supervised anomaly detector that combines two complementary plausibility estimates: a semantic score computed from separately encoded subject, relation, and object labels, and a relational score obtained through a relational graph convolutional network. The scores are standardized, calibrated, and fused. We evaluate the method on a subset of ICEWS18 with vocabulary-constrained synthetic an

ArXiv cs.LG.title: HIMX: mixed-format matrix multiplication based on customized HIFLOAT4 representations
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18641v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: 4-bit weight-activation quantization (W4A4) is an important approach for efficient large language model (LLM) inference. Recent hierarchical formats such as HiFloat4 (HIF4) improve the representational range of 4-bit quantization through multi-level scaling. However, the same local mantissa representation in HIF4 may not be equally suitable for weights and activations, which exhibit distinct distribution characteristics. To address this limitation, we propose HiMX, a mixed-mantissa framework built upon the hierarchical scaling structure of HIF4.

ArXiv cs.LG.title: FedFit: Federated Dynamic Sparse Training via Fisher Information scoring
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cross-device Federated Learning (FL) is frequently bottlenecked by the prohibitive memory and communication costs of training deep neural networks on resource-constrained edge hardware. While federated dynamic sparse training aims to alleviate these costs by adjusting sparse structures during training, existing methods rely on magnitude-based heuristics that are fundamentally ill-suited for the non-convergent, heterogeneous environments inherent to FL. To address this challenge, we propose FedFit, a federated dynamic sparse training framework th

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Minari: Infrastructure for Collaborative Reinforcement Learning Datasets
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) depends on shared datasets, but sharing them is still hard. Each benchmark ships its own format, documentation is thin, and most datasets cannot be regenerated once the environment code moves on. We introduce Minari, an open-source Python library for creating, sharing, and loading RL datasets. Its API follows Gymnasium, so recording a dataset means wrapping an environment and stepping through it as usual. From there, users can attach metadata, filter, combine, and shuffle datasets, and publish or download them

ArXiv cs.LG.title: RSIMed: Scaling Medical Foundation Models beyond Limited Clinical Data via Retrieval-Grounded Self-Evolution
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rare diseases are hard to diagnose, and the labeled clinical records needed to train models for them are few, private, and slow to extend, since a specialist must read every case. A model that writes its own training tasks could learn beyond these records, but no program can check a model-written diagnosis, and a wrong answer key corrupts training. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Screen Before You Add: Reducing Candidate Inference in Model Ensembles
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.18647v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As new models become available, existing ensembles must be updated to be competitive, making them intrinsically dynamic. Deciding whether to add a candidate model can require inference on an entire annotated dataset. Such a screening becomes prohibitive for models with costly inference especially when they ultimately add no value. Even under simple convex aggregation, relying on benchmark scores can be misleading as strong standalone performance does not guarantee ensemble improvement, and fitted ensemble weights can hurt test performance. The Verge AI.description: Google is rebranding its Spark AI agent as "Tasks" and making it free to use. The feature, which is powered by Google's new Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model, can do things like create meal plans, manage your calendar, and dig through your emails to find recurring expenses you might not need. The Verge AI.description: The Justice and Commerce Departments said that they are investigating Megaspeed, the Singapore-based data center company intertwined with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, after reporting suggested an investigation had been halted last year. The Verge AI.title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
The Verge AI.description: Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company's board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal. The Verge AI.title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
The Verge AI.description: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO. The Verge AI.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
The Verge AI.description: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters. The Verge AI.title: Sam Altman says he wants everyone ‘to have a lot of RAM’
The Verge AI.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is once again addressing his controversial comments on PC RAM purchases. "I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM, I think everybody should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer," Altman said today. "I think the home tinkering is great." […]

The Verge AI.title: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers
The Verge AI.description: Constellation Energy - America's largest operator of nuclear power plants - does not share Wall Street's concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. The Verge AI.title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
The Verge AI.description: Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions. The study homes in on hyperscale facilities - the […]

The Verge AI.title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
The Verge AI.description: Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors. Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on […]

The Verge AI.title: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines
The Verge AI.description: OpenAI is announcing a tool that it says will help child sexual abuse investigators cut through the noise to find harmful material they can act on quickly. At a Monday press briefing in Washington, DC, OpenAI announced a classifier it says can better detect abusive imagery of kids, including whether it's AI-generated. It's also offering […]

Wired AI.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
Wired AI.description: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.

Wired AI.title: The Apple Watch’s Live Rewind Can Record and Rewind Spoken Conversations. It’s Pretty Awkward
Wired AI.description: Live Rewind and Siri Recap can transcribe missed moments and summarize your day—if you don’t mind a little social clumsiness.

Wired AI.title: AI Told These Ex-Google Guys How to Build a Billion-Dollar Weapons Business
Wired AI.description: Google and Apple alumni Chad Steelberg and Andy Baynes are applying what they learned running software companies and designing iPhones to manufacturing lethal munitions.

Wired AI.title: Jensen Huang Is Gone. Now What?
Wired AI.description: After a shocking downfall, Nvidia’s CEO is out of a job. WIRED’s Lauren Goode explains what that means for the world’s most critical chip company, the AI industry, and Jensen Huang himself.

Wired AI.title: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess
Wired AI.description: AI competitors are catching up to Nvidia—and poised to take advantage of the chaos.

Wired AI.title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
Wired AI.description: YouTube Music and Spotify want synthetic hosts to curate your playlists. Their awkward banter and bogus song trivia are ruining the vibe.

Wired AI.title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets
Wired AI.description: A Carnegie Mellon student’s tiny E Ink gadgets, called OATs, give houseplants, skateboards, and dumbbells expressive personalities to nudge you toward better habits.

Wired AI.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
Wired AI.description: Fully automated ransomware hasn’t arrived—yet. But seemingly unsophisticated attackers are using AI tools to wreak havoc.

Wired AI.title: No Pilots. Few Air Traffic Controllers. What Could Go Wrong?
Wired AI.description: Normally, aviation is slow to embrace new technology—but AI has come for the skies.

Wired AI.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
Wired AI.description: The company says a bad update—not a cyberattack or AI—caused its servers around the world to crash.

MIT News — AI.title: Putting a spotlight on AI, society, and humanity
MIT News — AI.description: Supported by the MIT Human Insight Collaborative, scholars are exploring how AI is impacting the human experience and reshaping higher education.

MIT News — AI.title: Q&A: Why building math muscles remains important in the AI era
MIT News — AI.description: Assistant Professor John Urschel explains why learning the fundamental skills of mathematics is still essential despite the evolution of AI tools.

MIT News — AI.title: Learning the language of machine learning
MIT News — AI.description: By studying the computational foundations of language learning, Associate Professor Jacob Andreas builds intelligent systems that can communicate effectively with humans.

MIT News — AI.title: New AI “copilot” helps engineers design better structures
MIT News — AI.description: The system asks humans for feedback to increase trust in machine-generated designs for buildings and bridges.

MIT News — AI.title: Helping robots fit into the human workplace
MIT News — AI.description: Founded by Anthony Jules ’92, SM ’92 and Professor Emeritus Rodney Brooks, Robust AI’s robots are designed to collaborate with humans in factories and warehouses.

MIT News — AI.title: Three Lincoln Laboratory technologies receive 2026 R&D 100 Awards
MIT News — AI.description: A secure operating system, a quantum microsystem platform, and a 5G interference-canceling algorithm are named among the year's most significant innovations.

MIT News — AI.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
MIT News — AI.description: MIT scientists developed a training method to generate models that simulate the effects of human activities on climate much more quickly than other approaches.

MIT News — AI.title: MIT-led team receives funding to develop next-generation alternatives to modern weed killers
MIT News — AI.description: With up to $53 million from ARPA-H, the researchers will use AI to generate safer herbicides that reduce dependence on imports and improve the security of the U.S. food supply.

MIT News — AI.title: A single AI model simulates the behavior of many substances, from sliding sand to folding proteins
MIT News — AI.description: By learning how matter moves, the WorldParticle system could assist with developing soft robots, medicines, and more.

MIT News — AI.title: AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands
MIT News — AI.description: The new approach, known as FLEX, could lead to more intuitive, interactive household and assistive robots.

MIT News — AI.title: How to predict the behavior of molecules from scant data
MIT News — AI.description: A machine-learning approach called CheMeleon provides a practical way to develop new drugs or other molecules with much less detailed, expensive experimentation.

MIT News — AI.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
MIT News — AI.description: A new system identifies and corrects unreliable object descriptions stored in a robot’s memory, improving the robot’s ability to interact with its environment.

MIT News — AI.title: Building connections across the research infrastructure
MIT News — AI.description: MIT.nano and the Northeast Microelectronics Coalition gathered facility leaders and technology professionals from across the nation to explore ways to make shared-access facilities more connected.

MIT News — AI.title: Powering up for a pivotal moment
MIT News — AI.description: From a nuclear revival to qubits, the MIT Energy Initiative’s annual research conference tracked deployment of today’s technologies to discovery of tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

MIT News — AI.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
MIT News — AI.description: The MIT professors collaborated to identify the first AI-discovered antibiotic, a scientific breakthrough that is widely recognized as a milestone in AI-driven drug discovery.
